Endorsement.20: A letter of recommendation that you’ll need in order to participate in the Gym Challenge.

Wishing Star.20: A stone found in the Galar region with a mysterious power. It’s said that your dreams come true if you find one.

Dynamax Band.20: A Wishing Star has been affixed to it. It lets out a light that allows Pokémon to Dynamax when at a Power Spot.

Rotom Bike.20: This bike can do a turbo boost and run on the water using Rotom’s power. It’s a glistening black that shines reddish-black.

Sausages.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. These sausages should be boiled before eating.

Bob’s Food Tin.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. The tinned food that Bob sells is curiously popular in Galar.

Bach’s Food Tin.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. The tinned food that Bach sells is curiously popular in Galar.

Tin of Beans.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. When simmered, the beans suffuse a dish with their mild flavor.

Bread.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. An indispensable tool for mopping up that extra curry left on your plate.

Pasta.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. These flour noodles make for a surprisingly good match with curry.

Mixed Mushrooms.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. The chewy texture of the mushrooms transforms any dish they’re added to.

Smoke-Poke Tail.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. When a Slowpoke’s tail falls off, it grows back quickly.

Large Leek.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. Whether this is the kind of vegetable stalk that Farfetch’d like is unknown.

Fancy Apple.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. An apple chosen above others. It has spectacular form and a brilliant sheen.

Brittle Bones.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. The taste boiled off from the bones is sure to give a dish a light umami taste.

Pack of Potatoes.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. Potatoes help mellow out a spicy taste, to make a dish more mild.

Pungent Root.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. Though carelessly picked, these herbs can add a fragrant accent to a dish.

Salad Mix.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. The assortment of vegetables looks quite appealing and healthy.

Fried Food.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. It’s been a while since it was fried, so it’s gotten greasy.

Boiled Egg.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. Even just one boiled egg can really enhance a dish.

Camping Gear.20: Everything you need to set up a tent and get cooking in a Wild Area or at a camping spot.

Rusted Sword.20: It is said that a hero used this sword to halt a terrible disaster in ancient times. But it’s grown rusty and worn.

Rusted Shield.20: It is said that a hero used this shield to halt a terrible disaster in ancient times. But it’s grown rusty and worn.

Fossilized Bird.20: The fossil of an ancient Pokémon that once soared through the sky. What it looked like is a mystery.

Fossilized Fish.20: The fossil of an ancient Pokémon that once lived in the sea. What it looked like is a mystery.

Fossilized Drake.20: The fossil of an ancient Pokémon that once roamed the land. What it looked like is a mystery.

Fossilized Dino.20: The fossil of an ancient Pokémon that once lived in the sea. What it looked like is a mystery.

Strawberry Sweet.20: A strawberry-shaped sweet. When a Milcery holds this, it will spin around happily.

Love Sweet.20: A heart-shaped sweet. When a Milcery holds this, it spins around happily.

Berry Sweet.20: A berry-shaped sweet. When a Milcery holds this, it spins around happily.

Clover Sweet.20: A clover-shaped sweet. When a Milcery holds this, it spins around happily.

Flower Sweet.20: A flower-shaped sweet. When a Milcery holds this, it spins around happily.

Star Sweet.20: A star-shaped sweet. When a Milcery holds this, it spins around happily.

Ribbon Sweet.20: A ribbon-shaped sweet. When a Milcery holds this, it spins around happily.

Sweet Apple.20: A peculiar apple that can make a certain species of Pokémon evolve. It’s exceptionally sweet.

Tart Apple.20: A peculiar apple that can make a certain species of Pokémon evolve. It’s exceptionally tart.

Throat Spray.20: Raises Sp. Atk when a Pokémon uses a sound-based move.

Eject Pack.20: An item to be held by a Pokémon. When the holder’s stats are lowered, it will be switched out of battle.

Heavy-Duty Boots.20: These boots prevent the effects of traps set on the battlefield.

Blunder Policy.20: Raises Speed sharply when a Pokémon misses with a move because of accuracy.

Room Service.20: An item to be held by a Pokémon. Lowers Speed when Trick Room takes effect.

Utility Umbrella.20: An item to be held by a Pokémon. This sturdy umbrella protects the holder from the effects of rain and harsh sunlight.

Exp. Candy XS.20: A candy that is packed with energy. When consumed, it will grant a single Pokémon a very small amount of Exp. Points.

Exp. Candy S.20: A candy that is packed with energy. When consumed, it will grant a single Pokémon a small amount of Exp. Points.

Exp. Candy M.20: A candy that is packed with energy. When consumed, it will grant a single Pokémon a moderate amount of Exp. Points.

Exp. Candy L.20: A candy that is packed with energy. When consumed, it will grant a single Pokémon a large amount of Exp. Points.

Exp. Candy XL.20: A candy that is packed with energy. When consumed, it will grant a single Pokémon a very large amount of Exp. Points.

Dynamax Candy.20: A candy that is packed with energy. When consumed, it will raise the Dynamax Level of a single Pokémon by one. A higher level means higher HP when Dynamaxed.

TR00.20: A frenetic dance to uplift the fighting spirit. This sharply raises the user’s Attack stat.

TR01.20: The user drops onto the target with its full body weight. This may also leave the target with paralysis.

TR02.20: The target is scorched with an intense blast of fire. This may also leave the target with a burn.

TR03.20: The target is blasted by a huge volume of water launched under great pressure.

TR04.20: The user attacks everything around it by swamping its surroundings with a giant wave.

TR05.20: The target is struck with an icy-cold beam of energy. This may also leave the target frozen.

TR06.20: A howling blizzard is summoned to strike opposing Pokémon. This may also leave the opposing Pokémon frozen.

TR07.20: A powerful low kick that makes the target fall over. The heavier the target, the greater the move’s power.

TR08.20: A strong electric blast crashes down on the target. This may also leave the target with paralysis.

TR09.20: A wicked thunderbolt is dropped on the target to inflict damage. This may also leave the target with paralysis.

TR10.20: The user sets off an earthquake that strikes every Pokémon around it.

TR11.20: The target is hit by a strong telekinetic force. This may also lower the target’s Sp. Def stat.

TR12.20: The user relaxes and lightens its body to move faster. This sharply raises the Speed stat.

TR13.20: The user takes a deep breath and focuses so that critical hits land more easily.

TR14.20: The user waggles a finger and stimulates its brain into randomly using nearly any move.

TR15.20: The target is attacked with an intense blast of all-consuming fire. This may also leave the target with a burn.

TR16.20: The user charges at the target and may make it flinch.

TR17.20: The user temporarily empties its mind to forget its concerns. This sharply raises the user’s Sp. Def stat.

TR18.20: The user drains the target’s blood. The user’s HP is restored by half the damage taken by the target.

TR19.20: The user strikes with a simultaneous three-beam attack. This may also burn, freeze, or paralyze the target.

TR20.20: The user creates a substitute for itself using some of its HP. The substitute serves as the user’s decoy.

TR21.20: An all-out attack that becomes more powerful the less HP the user has.

TR22.20: Unsanitary sludge is hurled at the target. This may also poison the target.

TR23.20: The user lays a trap of spikes at the opposing team’s feet. The trap hurts Pokémon that switch into battle.

TR24.20: The user rampages and attacks for two to three turns. The user then becomes confused.

TR25.20: The user materializes an odd psychic wave to attack the target. This attack does physical damage.

TR26.20: The user endures any attack with at least 1 HP. Its chance of failing rises if it is used in succession.

TR27.20: While it is asleep, the user randomly uses one of the moves it knows.

TR28.20: Using its tough and impressive horn, the user rams into the target with no letup.

TR29.20: The user switches places with a party Pokémon in waiting and passes along any stat changes.

TR30.20: The user compels the target to keep using the move it encored for three turns.

TR31.20: The target is slammed with a steel-hard tail. This may also lower the target’s Defense stat.

TR32.20: The user crunches up the target with sharp fangs. This may also lower the target’s Defense stat.

TR33.20: The user hurls a shadowy blob at the target. This may also lower the target’s Sp. Def stat.

TR34.20: Two turns after this move is used, a hunk of psychic energy attacks the target.

TR35.20: The user attacks in an uproar for three turns. During that time, no Pokémon can fall asleep.

TR36.20: The user attacks by exhaling hot breath on opposing Pokémon. This may also leave those Pokémon with a burn.

TR37.20: The target is taunted into a rage that allows it to use only attack moves for three turns.

TR38.20: The user catches the target off guard and swaps its held item with its own.

TR39.20: The user attacks the target with great power. However, this also lowers the user’s Attack and Defense stats.

TR40.20: The user employs its psychic power to exchange Abilities with the target.

TR41.20: The user launches a kick that lands a critical hit more easily. This may also leave the target with a burn.

TR42.20: The user lets loose a horribly echoing shout with the power to inflict damage.

TR43.20: The user attacks the target at full power. The attack’s recoil harshly lowers the user’s Sp. Atk stat.

TR44.20: The user absorbs a mystical power from space to raise its Defense and Sp. Def stats.

TR45.20: The user attacks by shooting muddy water at opposing Pokémon. This may also lower their accuracy.

TR46.20: The user hardens its body’s surface like iron, sharply raising its Defense stat.

TR47.20: The user slashes the target with huge sharp claws.

TR48.20: The user tenses its muscles to bulk up its body, raising both its Attack and Defense stats.

TR49.20: The user quietly focuses its mind and calms its spirit to raise its Sp. Atk and Sp. Def stats.

TR50.20: The user handles a sharp leaf like a sword and attacks by cutting its target. Critical hits land more easily.

TR51.20: The user vigorously performs a mystic, powerful dance that raises its Attack and Speed stats.

TR52.20: The user tackles the target with a high-speed spin. The slower the user compared to the target, the greater the move’s power.

TR53.20: The user fights the target up close without guarding itself. This also lowers the user’s Defense and Sp. Def stats.

TR54.20: The user lays a trap of poison spikes at the feet of the opposing team. The spikes will poison opposing Pokémon that switch into battle.

TR55.20: The user cloaks itself in fire and charges the target. This also damages the user quite a lot. This attack may leave the target with a burn.

TR56.20: The user lets loose a blast of aura power from deep within its body at the target. This attack never misses.

TR57.20: The target is stabbed with a tentacle, arm, or the like steeped in poison. This may also poison the target.

TR58.20: The user releases a horrible aura imbued with dark thoughts. This may also make the target flinch.

TR59.20: The user slams a barrage of hard-shelled seeds down on the target from above.

TR60.20: The user slashes at the target by crossing its scythes or claws as if they were a pair of scissors.

TR61.20: The user generates a damaging sound wave by vibration. This may also lower the target’s Sp. Def stat.

TR62.20: The target is attacked with a shock wave generated by the user’s gaping mouth.

TR63.20: The user attacks with a ray of light that sparkles as if it were made of gemstones.

TR64.20: The user heightens its mental focus and unleashes its power. This may also lower the target’s Sp. Def stat.

TR65.20: The user draws power from nature and fires it at the target. This may also lower the target’s Sp. Def stat.

TR66.20: The user tucks in its wings and charges from a low altitude. This also damages the user quite a lot.

TR67.20: The user makes the ground under the target erupt with power. This may also lower the target’s Sp. Def stat.

TR68.20: The user stimulates its brain by thinking bad thoughts. This sharply raises the user’s Sp. Atk stat.

TR69.20: The user focuses its willpower to its head and attacks the target. This may also make the target flinch.

TR70.20: The user gathers all its light energy and releases it all at once. This may also lower the target’s Sp. Def stat.

TR71.20: The user whips up a storm of leaves around the target. The attack’s recoil harshly lowers the user’s Sp. Atk stat.

TR72.20: The user violently whirls its vines, tentacles, or the like to harshly lash the target.

TR73.20: The user shoots filthy garbage at the target to attack. This may also poison the target.

TR74.20: The user slams the target with its steel-hard head. This may also make the target flinch.

TR75.20: The user stabs the target from below with sharpened stones. Critical hits land more easily.

TR76.20: The user lays a trap of levitating stones around the opposing team. The trap hurts opposing Pokémon that switch into battle.

TR77.20: The user snares the target with grass and trips it. The heavier the target, the greater the move’s power.

TR78.20: The user strikes everything around it by swamping the area with a giant sludge wave. This may also poison those hit.

TR79.20: The user slams into the target with its heavy body. The more the user outweighs the target, the greater the move’s power.

TR80.20: The user hurls an electric orb at the target. The faster the user is than the target, the greater the move’s power.

TR81.20: The user turns the target’s power against it. The higher the target’s Attack stat, the greater the damage it deals.

TR82.20: The user attacks the target with stored power. The more the user’s stats are raised, the greater the move’s power.

TR83.20: The user teleports using a strange power and switches places with one of its allies.

TR84.20: The user shoots boiling hot water at its target. This may also leave the target with a burn.

TR85.20: The user is roused, and its Attack and Sp. Atk stats increase.

TR86.20: The user shrouds itself in electricity and smashes into its target. This also damages the user a little.

TR87.20: The user crashes into its target while rotating its body like a drill. Critical hits land more easily.

TR88.20: The user slams its target with its flame-covered body. The more the user outweighs the target, the greater the move’s power.

TR89.20: The user attacks by wrapping its opponent in a fierce wind that flies up into the sky. This may also confuse the target.

TR90.20: The user plays rough with the target and attacks it. This may also lower the target’s Attack stat.

TR91.20: Opposing Pokémon are drenched in an odd poisonous liquid. This lowers the Attack, Sp. Atk, and Speed stats of a poisoned target.

TR92.20: The user damages opposing Pokémon by emitting a powerful flash.

TR93.20: The user swings both arms and hits the target. The target’s stat changes don’t affect this attack’s damage.

TR94.20: The user fiercely attacks the target using its entire body.

TR95.20: The user attacks the target’s throat, and the resultant suffering prevents the target from using moves that emit sound for two turns.

TR96.20: The user attacks the enemy with a pollen puff that explodes. If the target is an ally, it gives the ally a pollen puff that restores its HP instead.

TR97.20: The user bites the target with its psychic capabilities. This can also destroy Light Screen and Reflect.

TR98.20: The user slams into the target using a full-force blast of water. This may also lower the target’s Defense stat.

TR99.20: The user attacks by slamming its body into the target. The higher the user’s Defense, the more damage it can inflict on the target.

TM00.20: The target is slugged by a punch thrown with muscle-packed power.

Lonely Mint.20: When a Pokémon smells this mint, its Attack will grow more easily, but its Defense will grow more slowly.

Wishing Piece.20: Throw one into a Pokémon Den to attract a wild Dynamax Pokémon.

Cracked Pot.20: A peculiar teapot that can make a certain species of Pokémon evolve. It may be cracked, but tea poured from it is delicious.

Chipped Pot.20: A peculiar teapot that can make a certain species of Pokémon evolve. It may be chipped, but tea poured from it is delicious.

Hi-tech Earbuds.20: Strange earbuds that allow you to freely control the volume of various sounds.

Fruit Bunch.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. The syrupy fruits give off a strong tropical feel.

Moomoo Cheese.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. Melted cheese can really give a curry some richness.

Spice Mix.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. There are over fifty spices contained within this ingredient’s hot flavor.

Fresh Cream.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. Add some whipped cream to a spicy curry to give it some sweetness.

Packaged Curry.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. Using packaged curry helps make sure there are no slipups when cooking.

Coconut Milk.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. The refined sweetness of this coconut milk makes it quite popular.

Instant Noodles.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. It has a junk-food sort of taste, but it goes well with curry.

Precooked Burger.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. If you’re unsure about what to cook, you can’t go wrong with some burger.

Gigantamix.20: One of the many ingredients that can be used for cooking at your camp. A mysterious spice. Even a tiny sprinkle is sure to make a curry gigantic.

Wishing Chip.20: Toss a number of them into a Pokémon Den for the chance to attract a wild Dynamax Pokémon.

Catching Charm.20: Holding it is said to increase the chance of getting a critical catch. Curiously, the charm doesn’t shake much.

Old Letter.20: A letter entrusted to you by a girl, to be delivered to a boy. Strangely, it looks old to you.

Band Autograph.20: It’s signed by all members of the Galar region’s most charismatic band, the Maximizers.

Sonia’s Book.20: Professor Sonia’s published writings. Her new discoveries about the Galar region’s legends are recorded in this enjoyable read.

Rotom Catalog.20: A catalog of devices that Rotom like. Use the catalog to have Rotom hop in and out of the various devices listed within.

Max Honey.20: Honey that Dynamax Vespiquen produces. Adding this honey to Max Soup makes the taste very smooth. It also has the same effect as a Max Revive.

Max Mushrooms.20: Mushrooms that have the power of changing Dynamax forms. They boost all stats of a Pokémon during battle.

Galarica Twig.20: A twig from a species of tree called Galarica that grows in certain areas around the Galar region. It’s a material for an accessory for a certain Pokémon.

Galarica Cuff.20: A cuff made from woven-together Galarica Twigs. Giving it to Galarian Slowpoke makes the Pokémon very happy.

Style Card.20: A card that increases the selection in boutiques and hair salons.

Armor Pass.20: A pass to go to the Isle of Armor. Show it to the rail staff at Wedgehurst Station.

Exp. Charm.20: A charm that increases the Exp. Points that Pokémon can get. A machine-like object is inside the charm.

Armorite Ore.20: Rare ore that can be obtained on the Isle of Armor. Something good will happen if you give it to a collector on the Isle of Armor.

Mark Charm.20: A mysterious and unique charm that increases the chance of finding a Pokémon with a mark.

Reins of Unity.20: Cords that shine when you hold them up to the light. The people of old times presented these to the King of Bountiful Harvests to express their gratitude.

Galarica Wreath.20: A wreath made from woven-together Galarica Twigs. Placing it on the head of a Galarian Slowpoke makes the Pokémon very happy.

Legendary Clue 1.20: A clue about the King of Bountiful Harvests. It’s written by Peony, and an old photo is attached to it.

Legendary Clue 2.20: A clue about the legend of giants. It’s written by Peony and has unique drawings.

Legendary Clue 3.20: A clue about the legend of bird Pokémon. It’s written by Peony and has a unique drawing.

Legendary Clue?.20: A mysterious clue that Peony seems to have dropped. There’s a photo attached to it showing a shining hole opening above the Max Lair.

Crown Pass.20: A pass to go to the Crown Tundra. Show it to the rail staff at Wedgehurst Station.

Wooden Crown.20: A mysterious object made of wood. Part of it seems to be chipped. Maybe it’s meant to be part of something.

Radiant Petal.20: A single petal that the King of Bountiful Harvests gave you. It radiates faint light.

White Mane Hair.20: Mane hair that belonged to the King of Bountiful Harvests’ beloved steed, Glastrier. The hair is strong and very flexible.

Black Mane Hair.20: Mane hair that belonged to the King of Bountiful Harvests’ beloved steed, Spectrier. The hair is very smooth to the touch.

Iceroot Carrot.20: Produce that the King of Bountiful Harvests’ beloved steed likes to eat. It grew in a field covered in snow.

Shaderoot Carrot.20: Produce that the King of Bountiful Harvests’ beloved steed likes to eat. It grew in a gloomy field.

Dynite Ore.20: Mysterious ore that can be obtained in the Max Lair. Something good will happen if you give it to a collector in the Crown Tundra.

Carrot Seeds.20: Seeds to plant in a field. The kind of carrot you’ll get is determined by which field you plant the seeds in.

Ability Patch.20: A patch that allows a Pokémon with a regular Ability to have a rare Ability.

Leaden Ball.24: Upgraded version of the Heavy Ball. Doesn't fly far, but is more effective if the Pokémon hasn't noticed the player.

Gigaton Ball.24: Upgraded version of the Leaden Ball. Doesn't fly far, but is more effective if the Pokémon hasn't noticed the player.

Feather Ball.24: Can be thrown further than a regular Poké Ball. Is more effective for catching Pokémon that fly high in the air.

Wing Ball.24: Can be thrown further than a Feather Ball. Is more effective for catching Pokémon that fly high in the air.

Jet Ball.24: Can be thrown further than a Wing Ball. Is more effective for catching Pokémon that fly high in the air.
